figures.title: The head: h to V logits to a distribution
figures.caption: The head projects the final hidden state h of width d_model into one score per vocabulary entry with s = h·Wᵀ, then softmax turns those scores into a distribution. For three candidates scoring 2, 1 and 0, the exponentials are 7.389, 2.718 and 1, summing to 11.107, and the probabilities are 0.665, 0.245 and 0.090. At d_model = 4,096 and V = 50,000 the projection performs d_model·V = 204,800,000 multiply-adds, or 2·d_model·V FLOPs, comparable to a 4d feedforward layer's 12·d_model² ≈ 201,300,000.
figures.alt: Five lanes across five steps. Step one is the final hidden vector h of width 4,096. Steps two and three score three candidate tokens A, B and C with logits 2, 1 and 0, then exponentiate them to 7.389, 2.718 and 1. A separate lane sums those exponentials to 11.107 in step four, and step five divides each by the sum, giving 0.665, 0.245 and 0.090. The probabilities are outlined as the new cells.

data.note: Only the gaps between logits matter: shifting all three scores by the same amount cancels from every term. Implementations subtract the largest logit before exponentiating, which leaves the distribution unchanged and keeps e^s from overflowing. The 204,800,000 and 201,300,000 figures are multiply-add counts per token.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to project h and normalise the scores.

steps.label: h is the last residual-stream vector, d_model wide.
Each vocabulary row of Wᵀ scores h: three candidates get 2, 1 and 0.
Exponentiate each score; the gaps become ratios.
Divide by the sum; the probabilities are 0.665, 0.245 and 0.090.

figures.title: Temperature reshapes the same three logits
figures.caption: Temperature divides every logit before softmax and leaves the order unchanged. On the same logits 2, 1 and 0, T = 0.5 sharpens the distribution to 0.867 / 0.117 / 0.016, T = 1 gives 0.665 / 0.245 / 0.090, and T = 2 flattens it to 0.506 / 0.307 / 0.186. Row 1 is T = 1. Each cell is a probability, inked in proportion to its value.
figures.alt: A four-column table with three rows. The first column names the temperature: 0.5, 1 and 2. The next three columns are the probabilities assigned to candidates with logits 2, 1 and 0. At T = 0.5 the row reads 0.867, 0.117, 0.016; at T = 1, 0.665, 0.245, 0.090; at T = 2, 0.506, 0.307, 0.186. The ink in each cell grows with its probability, so the first column darkens as temperature falls.

data.note: At T = 0.5 the scaled logits are 4, 2 and 0, with exponentials 54.598, 7.389 and 1 summing to 62.987. At T = 2 they are 1, 0.5 and 0, with 2.718, 1.649 and 1 summing to 5.367. Temperature can only reweight what the head already produced; it cannot recover a candidate scored far below the top.

sources.note: Press and Wolf, Using the Output Embedding to Improve Language Models (2016): tying W to the input embedding E makes the score for candidate w equal to h·e_w.
Hinton, Vinyals and Dean, Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network (2015): temperature-scaled softmax and the T² factor in the distillation loss.
